## What's new

- **YouTube.** Send a YouTube video, Short, finished live stream or YouTube Music song to Dowlio and pick a quality, from 144p up to 4K, or Audio only. Each download is one file with sound, in the video's original language. Dubbed languages are listed as their own audio choices.
- **Playlists and albums.** Send a playlist or a YouTube Music album, untick what you don't want, and choose one quality for all of it. The videos download 3 at a time into a numbered folder named after the playlist.
- **Many more sites.** When Dowlio can't find a video on a page, it can ask yt-dlp, which reads hundreds of video sites. YouTube players embedded in other pages are found too.
- **Subtitles, Chapters and Cover art.** Turn on Download subtitles in Settings › Downloads to get subtitles in your languages inside the file. Chapters and the video's thumbnail go in automatically.
- **Above 1080p and WebM.** Video above 1080p is saved as MP4 on Macs that play AV1 in hardware, and as WebM elsewhere. Sites that only serve WebM now download too.
- **Downloads that last.** A YouTube download paused overnight gets fresh links on its own and carries on.

## Two free tools

Dowlio reads YouTube with **yt-dlp** (github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp), a free open-source tool, and **QuickJS-NG** (github.com/quickjs-ng/quickjs), which yt-dlp uses to run YouTube's scripts. The first time a site needs them, Dowlio asks before downloading them from their GitHub pages, about 56 MB. Dowlio checks each against the hash published with it and never runs a copy that has changed. You can also install, update or remove them in Settings › Downloads › Tools, or while setting up Dowlio.

Dowlio now includes FFmpeg, built without any GPL or non-free parts, to join video it can't join with macOS alone. It never re-encodes your video or audio. The About window credits it.

## Before you update

- **Allow the keychain prompt.** After this update, macOS asks once whether Dowlio may read its saved browser pairings. Choose Always Allow. Your browsers stay paired.
